name: Angola
tagline: The Kalandula falls, and a coast nobody has seen
summary: Kalandula is one of the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume, the Namib runs up the whole southern coast to the Iona dunes, and Luanda's bay is closed by a sand spit with the Atlantic on the other side of it.
when: The cacimbo, May to September — dry and cooler, and the roads are passable.

entries.caption: Kalandula
entries.description: A hundred and five metres of water across four hundred, in the middle of nowhere.
entries.subject: the wide curtain of the Kalandula falls in Malanje

entries.caption: The Black Rocks and the Namib
entries.description: Pungo Andongo's monoliths in the north, and the Namib running the whole southern coast.
entries.subject: the black monoliths of Pungo Andongo standing over grassland

entries.caption: Giant Sable
entries.description: The palanca negra gigante lives in Angola and nowhere else, and was thought extinct until 2004.
entries.subject: a giant sable antelope with long curved horns in miombo woodland

entries.caption: Kissama and Luengue-Luiana
entries.description: Kissama two hours from Luanda, restocked and recovering; the southeast on the Okavango's headwaters.
entries.subject: elephants in open woodland in Kissama National Park

entries.caption: Mount Moco
entries.description: 2,620 metres in the Huambo highlands, with the last Afromontane forest in the country on it.
entries.subject: the grassy summit of Mount Moco above patches of forest

entries.caption: Kalandula and Ruacana
entries.description: Kalandula in Malanje, and the Ruacana falls on the Cunene where Namibia begins.
entries.subject: water thundering over the Ruacana falls on the Cunene

entries.caption: The Kwanza and the Cunene
entries.description: The Kwanza runs to the Atlantic below Luanda; the Cunene is the Namibian border.
entries.subject: the wide Kwanza river running to the Atlantic

entries.caption: Sixteen Hundred Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: The Ilha at Luanda, the Mussulo lagoon, and the dune coast running south to Iona.
entries.subject: the sand spit of the Ilha do Cabo curving across Luanda bay

entries.caption: Maiombe
entries.description: Angola's Amazon — rainforest in the Cabinda exclave, north of the Congo river.
entries.subject: dense rainforest canopy in the Maiombe forest of Cabinda

entries.caption: The Southern Desert
entries.description: Iona, the Tundavala gap and the escarpment road down to Namibe.
entries.subject: the sheer escarpment and drop at the Tundavala gap

entries.caption: Semba, Kizomba and Kuduro
entries.description: Semba became samba across the Atlantic, and kuduro went back the other way.
entries.subject: dancers and a sound system at a kuduro party in Luanda

entries.caption: Ovimbundu, Mbundu, Bakongo, Ovahimba
entries.description: Ovimbundu in the centre, Bakongo in the north, and Ovahimba along the Cunene.
entries.subject: an Ovahimba woman in ochre and braided hair near the Cunene

entries.caption: Funge, Muamba and Calulu
entries.description: Funge with muamba de galinha, calulu with dried fish, and Portuguese pastries after.
entries.subject: a plate of muamba de galinha with funge

entries.caption: Carnaval da Vitoria
entries.description: Luanda's carnival on the Marginal, with the neighbourhood groups competing.
entries.subject: carnival dancers in costume on Luanda's Marginal

entries.caption: The Pensador and Basketry
entries.description: The Chokwe Thinker is the national symbol, and Chokwe masks and chairs are among Africa's finest.
entries.subject: a carved Chokwe Thinker figure in dark wood

entries.caption: Mbanza Kongo
entries.description: The capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, and the first sub-Saharan city to have a stone cathedral.
entries.subject: the ruined stone cathedral walls at Mbanza Kongo

entries.caption: Mbanza Kongo, Listed
entries.description: Inscribed in 2017 as the seat of a kingdom that dealt with Portugal as an equal.
entries.subject: the archaeological site and old walls at Mbanza Kongo

entries.caption: Luanda and Benguela
entries.description: A bay closed by a sand spit and a skyline that went up fast, and a quieter colonial port south.
entries.subject: Luanda's high-rise skyline curving round the bay

entries.caption: Portuguese Colonial and Modernist
entries.description: Fortaleza de Sao Miguel, Benguela's pastel streets, and Luanda's late-modernist blocks.
entries.subject: the yellow walls of the Fortaleza de Sao Miguel above Luanda

entries.caption: The Marginal at Six
entries.description: The whole city walks and runs the bay road in the evening, and keeps doing it after dark.
entries.subject: people walking and running the Marginal in Luanda at dusk

entries.caption: The Mussulo
entries.description: A lagoon behind the spit south of Luanda, calm, shallow and full of families at weekends.
entries.subject: families in shallow lagoon water at the Mussulo

entries.caption: The Escarpment Roads
entries.description: Serra da Leba's hairpins, and Tundavala where the plateau simply stops.
entries.subject: the hairpin bends of the Serra da Leba pass from above

entries.caption: Luanda, and Little Else
entries.description: Good hotels in the capital, and very little organised outside it.
entries.subject: a hotel terrace looking over Luanda bay at sunset

entries.caption: Bringing the Sable Back
entries.description: The giant sable was found alive in 2004 and has been fenced, guarded and bred since.
entries.subject: a ranger monitoring giant sable in a fenced sanctuary

entries.caption: Water and Rock
entries.description: Kalandula in the wet season, when the spray reaches the viewpoint.
entries.subject: spray rising from the Kalandula falls in full flow

entries.caption: Tundavala
entries.description: A gap in the escarpment where the ground drops a thousand metres, with no railing.
entries.subject: a figure at the edge of the Tundavala gap looking down

entries.caption: Why Angola
entries.description: A waterfall to rival Victoria's, a desert coast, and a capital that surprises everyone.
entries.subject: the Kalandula falls with nobody at the viewpoint
